title: Ancient Civilisations
summary: Explore how early societies organised themselves, traded, and built enduring legacies.

events.title: Building the Great Pyramid of Giza
events.summary: Skilled labourers organised massive stone blocks to create a royal tomb that signalled the power of the Old Kingdom.
knownFacts: The pyramid was built for Pharaoh Khufu during Egypt's Fourth Dynasty.
Workers used sleds, ramps, and levers to move limestone blocks.
Skilled workers lived in planned villages near the site, not enslaved masses.

sceneDefaults.people: team of Egyptian builders and overseers

events.title: Athens Democratic Assembly
events.summary: Citizens gathered to debate and vote on laws that shaped classical Athens.
knownFacts: Only free male citizens could vote; women, enslaved people, and foreigners were excluded.
Meetings occurred on the Pnyx hill with speakers addressing the crowd.
Voting often used raised hands or broken pottery shards (ostraka).

title: Industrial Revolution
summary: Mechanisation reshaped work, cities, and global trade in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries.

events.title: Cotton Mill Workday
events.summary: Water- and steam-powered machines increased textile output but created harsh factory conditions.
knownFacts: Early mills employed entire families, including children, for long shifts.
Arkwright and others used water frames and spinning mules to automate spinning.
Factory towns grew rapidly around rivers and canals.

events.title: Early Steam Railway
events.summary: Steam locomotives linked coalfields and cities, speeding goods and people across new rail lines.
knownFacts: Stephenson's Rocket popularised the use of multi-tube boilers for speed.
Railways required tunnels, bridges, and stations built by navvies.
Coal smoke and cinders affected passengers and nearby towns.

sceneDefaults.location: rural rail line with early station
sceneDefaults.objects: steam locomotive, coal tender, semaphore signal

title: Cold War & Decolonisation
summary: Nations navigated ideological rivalry and independence movements after World War II.

events.title: Berlin Airlift
events.summary: Western Allies flew supplies into West Berlin after the Soviet blockade of land routes.
knownFacts: Allied planes landed every few minutes with coal, food, and medicine.
Children waited for candy parachutes dropped by pilots.
The operation demonstrated commitment to West Berlin without direct conflict.

events.title: Decolonisation Rally
events.summary: Citizens organised peaceful rallies and negotiations to demand independence and self-rule.
knownFacts: Student groups, unions, and community leaders often coordinated demonstrations.
Symbolic flags, banners, and songs expressed national identity.
Protests were often met with censorship or arrests, but many remained peaceful.
